item.title: Boston Celtics at Houston Rockets: Stream, lineups, injury reports, broadcast (11/2)
item.description: The Boston Celtics are on a five-game winning streak, but all of those wins were earned against teams with losing records. It's still early in the season, so one or two of the aforementioned opponents should finish above .500. But, for now, Boston hasn't faced a top seed. That could all change on Monday night, as the 5-1 Celtics take on the 6-1 Houston Rockets in Texas. It'll be a tough task for the C's, who just played on Sunday night in Florida, securing a 108-97 road win over the undermanned Orlando Magic . However, the Celtics are already 1-0 on the second night of a back-to-back this season and have typically played well with limited rest under head coach Joe Mazzulla. As for the Rockets, they last played on Friday evening at the Toyota Center, where they crushed the Oklahoma City Thunder , 119-98. No injury report is out yet for the Celtics, yet they should expect a challenging game no matter who is active. Records, standing, and streaks Following a frustrating loss in the regular-season opener versus the Detroit Pistons , the Celtics have won five games in a row. That matches their longest winning streak from last season, and they currently find themselves in third place in the Eastern Conference at 5-1. Meanwhile, the Rockets are coming off a double-digit win against the Thunder and sit in second place in the Western Conference at 6-1. Player injuries The Celtics haven't posted an injury report yet. But, it's worth noting that guard Devin Carter has missed every game this season due to illness (mononucleosis). Center Mitchell Robinson was sidelined for the Celtics' most recent outing due to rest, but perhaps he returns for the second leg of the back-to-back set of games. The Rockets have multiple injuries to report. Steven Adams (right soleus strain) is out while Clint Capela (right ankle sprain) and Reed Sheppard (low back strain) are questionable. item.title: Notre Dame Prep girls soccer wins second straight SWC title, and its fifth in six years
item.description: Notre Dame Prep girls soccer defeated Pomperaug 4-0 to claim its second straight SWC title and its fifth in six years. The Lancers won the championship at WestConn on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. (Will Aldam/Hearst Connecticut Media) DANBURY - When it comes to girls soccer in the SWC, one team stands above the rest. Notre Dame Prep successfully defended its conference title on Sunday, defeating Pomperaug 4-0 at Western Connecticut State University for its fifth SWC title in six years. "We just keep getting good players that come to the school, and it is all about the players," Notre Dame Prep coach Wayne Mones said. "They want to play for us, they want to learn and they want to get better. If they want to be a champion, they come to Notre Dame." Notre Dame Prep has reached the SWC championship game in six straight seasons, only losing in 2024 to Brookfield. Lancers goalie Cara Williams was named the tournament MVP after posing three shutouts, not allowing a goal in the tournament. Notre Dame Prep outscored opponents 11-0 in the three games. "I feel really great, I honestly couldn't do this without my teammates," Williams said. "They always help me get better and this just feels really good. "This really shows how great we are. Wayne (Mones) is a great coach, he strives to win. And all of these girls are so determined, from my freshman year to now it is amazing how much we have succeeded." Junior forward Kolbe McCray scored a pair of goals in the championship game, while Maria Rocha Reaes and Truth Houston also scored. McCray scored the second and final goal for the Lancers. "It is fun, being a forward and getting to score (in a championship game), I enjoy it," McCray said. "My team makes it fun for me too, they know how to move the ball and they always find me. I am proud of everybody, and I am proud to do it for my team." Pomperaug reached its first SWC championship game since 2018 by defeating Newtown in penalties in the semifinals. Notre Dame Prep will now turn its attention to the CIAC Class LL tournament, hoping to reach its first final since 2023. Player of the Game Kolbe McCray, Notre Dame Prep: The junior scored a pair of goals to help lead the Lancers to a 4-0 championship victory over Pomperaug. Quotable "That has been our staple all year, we have only allowed four goals on the season. Our defense has been great and Cara Williams, our goalie, has been great. But offensively we have done well also, we score a lot of goals." - Wayne Mones Notre Dame Prep 4, Pomperaug 0 (at WestConn) POMPERAUG 0 0 - 0 NOTRE DAME 1 3 - 4 Scoring: ND: Maria Rocha Reaes (PEN), 21:15; ND: Kolbe McCray, 60:54; ND: Truth Houston (Siena Rosa), 72:16; ND: Kolbe McCray, 79:20. item.title: ‘We moved as a unit’- Kevin Durant reflects on Thunder’s early identity
item.description: Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images Kevin Durant has looked back on the Oklahoma City Thunder’s early years, recalling how a young group of teammates built a strong connection both on and off the basketball court. Now with the Houston Rockets, Durant spoke to ESPN about the unusual road-trip routine that saw several Thunder players exploring shopping malls together while wearing matching team clothing. Oklahoma City was still finding its feet as an NBA franchise when Durant and his teammates began developing the relationships that would shape the team’s identity. Kevin Durant recalls how the young Oklahoma City Thunder stuck together Durant remembered how the group would spend time together after arriving in different cities during road trips. “I can remember early on, our first few years, every time we went on a road trip, we would land and six or seven of us would go through to the mall in every city together, it’s crazy to think about it, with Oklahoma City Thunder sweats on,” Durant said. The image of several NBA players walking around a shopping centre in matching Thunder clothing offers a glimpse into how close the group became during its early years. For Durant, those moments represented more than simply spending time together away from basketball. They reflected the shared identity that was developing within the team. “But we moved as a unit, and people understood that about us,” Durant said. “We were young and energetic. And that matched the franchise in Oklahoma City itself.” Durant also reflected on the welcome the franchise received when it arrived in Oklahoma City in 2008. Despite being a rebuilding team, the Thunder found a passionate fanbase that embraced the players before they had established themselves as contenders. “With open arms. The excitement, the energy level was high,” Durant said. “We weren’t a great team. We were a young team in rebuilding mode. But you wouldn’t have thought that from listening and hearing the fans around the city once we got there.” He added: “You could tell that region was waiting for a professional team to come. And I felt right at home early.” Durant’s recollections highlight the connection between the players and the city during the franchise’s formative years. Before the team’s biggest achievements, a sense of togetherness was already taking shape, both inside the locker room and throughout Oklahoma City. item.title: Victor Wembanyama reveals the biggest lesson he learned from Gregg Popovich
item.description: Victor Wembanyama reveals the biggest lesson he learned from Gregg Popovich originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama has cemented himself as one of the best players in the league over the past three years. He only arrived in 2023, but he has quickly developed star qualities that have helped the San Antonio Spurs go from a team on the outside looking in to becoming a championship contender. The credit is certainly deservedly going to Wembanyama, but there are also a lot of people behind the scenes who have played important roles. One is Gregg Popovich, who was Wembanyama's coach early in his career, but has transitioned into a more front office role in recent years. Gregg Popovich has a massive impact on Victor Wembanyama's career Popovich is one of the most influential figures over the past three decades of NBA basketball. He was the mastermind behind the Spurs ' dominance from the 1990s all the way to the late 2010s. He and Tim Duncan formed a partnership that eventually led to them winning five championships together. Even though players like Duncan and Tony Parker retired, Popovich maintained his role with the Spurs as the head honcho. That changed when he encountered health problems at the tail end of his coaching career. However, he still managed to help develop a megastar on his way out of his head coach job. MORE: Victor Wembanyama gets honest about his problems on the offensive side of the game Wembanyama himself is glad to have worked with Popovich. To this day, Pop still has an impact on Wembanyama and the rest of the Spurs, but the team's superstar credits the five-time champion coach for helping him adjust to the NBA. "He often said something when we were in film: after a win, you're rarely as good as you thought you were, and after a loss, you're rarely as bad as you thought you were," Wembanyama said on 60 Minutes about Popovich's impact on him . As long as Popovich remains with the Spurs in his role, he will have an impact on the players. Everyone, including Wembanyama, has always raved about him and his role behind the scenes, so he will continue to influence the next generation of Spurs basketball as long as he is there. item.title: Jonathan Taylor trade rumor details Broncos’ hot pursuit of Colts RB
item.description: The Denver Broncos are reportedly in hot pursuit of a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor . The rumor comes from Zac Stevens of DNVR Broncos , who says the Broncos are “going to try to pull this trade off” because “they want Jonathan Taylor now.” Stevens adds that a trade “could happen at any moment.” “I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor. This could happen at any moment. You might not want to go to sleep Broncos Country,” Stevens said. MORE: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Grading every deal, top available candidates “The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now,” Stevens added. Stevens isn’t the first reporter to confirm the Broncos are interested in Taylor. On Saturday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that the Broncos are among the teams to have inquired about Taylor. “The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and New York Giants, sources said,” Rapoport and Schefter wrote. MORE: Jonathan Taylor trade rumor reveals Colts’ asking price The Colts were initially hesitant to trade Taylor, per reports, but as the ESPN reporters included in the aforementioned report, Indy’s stance has changed. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman, the latter of whom has been coming on strong of late. However, Harvey is now on injured reserve and Taylor is one of the best running backs in the entire NFL and would amount to a huge upgrade for Denver’s offense. It makes all the sense in the world for the Broncos to go get the former rushing champion, who would also make quarterback Bo Nix’s life much easier. How much will Jonathan Taylor cost? That deal saw the Panthers get a second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round pick for the superstar running back. We suspect the Colts will end up getting half of that package, and more specifically a second-round pick and a Day 3 selection, but that’s just a guess, of course. Michael Penix Jr. had a brutal performance to forget following the Atlanta Falcons’ 16-0 shutout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday afternoon. Penix is halfway through the third season of his NFL career with the Falcons. Injuries and inconsistent play have limited his production on the field, but he has showed his potential as a dynamic quarterback when healthy. However, the Week 8 contest wasn’t one of those games for him. Severe weather conditions impacted how both teams played throughout the day, especially Penix. He only completed eight out of 24 passes for 125 yards and four interceptions while rushing five times for 11 yards. These numbers were so negative that his quarterback rating was worse than Baker Mayfield’s, who only attempted three passes. How Michael Penix Jr., Falcons played against Buccaneers Michael Penix Jr. knows that he isn’t fully at fault for his performance given the weather conditions. However, he will have to move on from this game as soon as possible to get Atlanta’s offense back on track after losing to the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay mainly relied on three field goals throughout the game. They got the only touchdown of the day in the third quarter, seeing the running backs shine as the top offensive players of the contest. Bijan Robinson was the lone bright spot in Atlanta’s offense. Atlanta fell to a 3-5 record this season, sitting at third place in the NFC South Division standings. They are above the New Orleans Saints while trailing the Buccaneers and the Carolina Panthers. (Photo by Kai Kanzer/Texas Rangers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Texas Rangers infielder/outfielder Ezequiel Duran has been named the American League winner of the Gold Glove Award for the utility position. It is Duran’s first time winning a Gold Glove award. Duran entered spring training fighting for a bench role on the major league roster before being an invaluable regular presence in the team’s 2026 lineup. Duran played all over the field, with 49 starts at shortstop, 41 at third base, 25 at second base, 14 in center field, nine in left field, seven in right field, and one at third base. His versatility led to his being dubbed “the Solution.” Duran was one of four Gold Glove finalists on the Rangers, with Wyatt Langford, Evan Carter and Jacob deGrom being the other three. item.title: UConn football falls at Air Force 35-26
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Colorado Springs, Colorado, USA; Air Force Falcons fullback Kemper Hodges (4) pitches the ball in the third quarter against the UConn Huskies at Falcon Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UConn football couldn’t handle the Air Force option attack, allowing 366 rushing yards in a 35-26 loss to fall to 4-4 on the season. Air Force QB Kemper Hodges ran for 200 yards and four touchdowns as the Falcons dominated the second half on their way to victory after starting the game with a 14-0 lead. The Huskies hit some big plays across the day but didn’t get enough chances with the ball as Air Force drained over 20 minutes off the clock in two touchdown drives. On the day, Air Force converted 5-of-6 fourth-down attempts, notching 23 first downs along the way. After falling behind early, UConn made some stops and gained a touchdown in the second quarter with two sustained drives that saw QB Kalieb Osborne connect deep in big moments. In the third quarter, Air Force kept a drive alive with a fake punt and scored a touchdown to push the lead back to 14. UConn nearly closed in with a couple of big plays, a 55-yard touchdown pass to TE Alex Godavitarne and a 46-yard run by Kenji Christian. A missed extra point after the long TD pass pushed UConn to go for two after the Christian run. Osborne was sacked on the attempt, making it 28-26. Air Force closed out the game with an 11:37 touchdown drive that had three third-down conversions and two fourth-down conversions, including the Hodges touchdown run from one yard out to go up by nine. With its last-ditch effort, the defensive pressure was too much for UConn as four passes fell incomplete to effectively end the game. Air Force reached bowl eligibility with its sixth win of the season. Next up, UConn faces North Carolina at Rentschler Field. The game kicks off at 12 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network.

After the Minnesota Vikings ’ 19-15 loss to Detroit, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell opened his postgame press conference with a heartfelt message for injured Lions linebacker Jack Campbell , making it clear that the frightening incident mattered far more than the result. O’Connell addressed the injury before discussing the Vikings’ performance, offering his support for the Lions linebacker and his teammates. “Want to start out and just mention we’re all thinking and praying for Jack Campbell,” O’Connell told reporters, via FOX Sports. He was placed on a backboard and carted off before being taken to a local hospital for evaluation of a neck injury. The concern extended throughout Detroit’s locker room. Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams described the scene as painful for the organization, emphasizing Campbell’s importance as a team captain and leader. Williams said the team drew motivation from the moment, wanting to keep fighting for their injured teammate. Detroit may have walked away with the 19-15 divisional victory, but the result quickly took a backseat to concerns over Campbell’s condition. item.title: Brewers' Brice Turang, Jackson Chourio win Rawlings Gold Glove Awards
item.description: For the second time in three years – and only the third time ever – two Milwaukee Brewers have been recognized as the top defenders at their respective positions. Second baseman Brice Turang and left fielder Jackson Chourio were named Rawlings Gold Glove Award winners in the National League on Sunday, Nov. 1. It was Turang's second Gold Glove and Chourio's first. Turang, who won his first Gold Glove in 2024 and was earned a Platinum Glove as the top overall defender in the NL, becomes the third Brewers player to win multiple awards and the first since first baseman Cecil Cooper in 1979 and 1980. The 26-year-old, who beat out fellow finalists Brandon Lowe of the Pittsburgh Pirates and JJ Wetherholt of the St. Louis Cardinals , finished fifth in the majors among all players with 19 defensive runs saved and sixth with 14 defensive runs saved as measured by Major League Baseball. Turang also finished second in the majors and first among all infielders with 23 defensive runs saved, a differing metric. All three represent career highs for the fourth-year pro who is also coming off a monster year at the plate and is certain to earn some down-ballot votes for the NL Most Valuable Player Award. Turang remains the only second baseman in Brewers history to win a Gold Glove. Chourio, meanwhile, beat out four-time winner Ian Happ of the Chicago Cubs and Daylen Lile of the Washington Nationals after turning in what rated as easily the third-year pro's best defensive season. Chourio, 22, ranked 48th in the majors among all players with seven outs above average and 39th with seven runs prevented. Among left fielders, Chourio's seven outs above average were one behind the majors' leader, Chandler Simpson of the Tampa Bay Rays. With 13 defensive runs saved, Chourio finished 14th overall, seventh among all outfielders and second among left fielders. Chourio also had eight outfield assists. The Gold Glove represents a major step forward for Chourio, who had rated out as average to slightly above average in his previous two seasons. Chourio is the fifth Brewers outfielder to win a Gold Glove, joining Sal Frelick in 2024, Lorenzo Cain in 2019, Carlos Gómez in 2013 and Sixto Lezcano in 1979. Un par de arremetidas del ‘Toro’, así como una buena intervención del arquero García a un disparo de larga distancia de Piovi, fueron lo más destacado de una primera mitad en la que quedó demostrado porque el León es una de las mejores defensivas del certamen. Fue al 56′ que los locales lograron abrir el marcador, tras una falta en el área sobre Charly Rodríguez que Andrés Montaño se encargó de transformar en gol. El quinto gol del torneo para el mexicano, que vive el mejor momento de su carrera. Desde entonces, Cruz Azul fue amo y señor del partido, pero le faltó precisión en el último pase para sentenciar el compromiso ante La Fiera. Fue al 76′ que lograron ampliar la ventaja con una gran jugada colectiva que José Paradela, con un desvío de la zaga, marcó para el 2-0 en su regreso a las canchas tras estar fuera durante varias semanas por lesión. Los celestes tuvieron varias oportunidades para poner el 3-0, pero erraron en la última zona y les terminó costando caro sobre el final, pues al 90+10′ se señaló un penal sobre Alfonso Alvarado, misma que el propio ‘Plátano’ convirtió en gol para poner el 2-1 definitivo. De esta forma, Cruz Azul llegó a 29 puntos, mismas que América y Chivas, y se colocó en el tercer lugar de la tabla por diferencia de goles. Mientras que el León se ubicó en la séptima posición con 22 puntos y buscarán amarrar su boleto a la Fiesta Grande en las últimas jornadas.

(Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich is beginning to plan for a potentially major change in goal, with Manuel Neuer’s future becoming one of the key decisions ahead of next season, per Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg (via @iMiaSanMia ). Neuer is increasingly expected to retire in the summer, although no final decision has been made yet. Whatever happens with the legendary goalkeeper will have a major influence on how Bayern approaches the position. One thing appears increasingly clear: Bayern Munich sees Jonas Urbig as the goalkeeper it wants to move forward with. Rather than signing another young goalkeeper who could immediately compete with Urbig for the starting role, the club wants an experienced and loyal No. 2 who understands and accepts his role within the squad. Bayern Munich currently has 7–8 candidates under consideration, but there have been no concrete talks with any of them at this stage. The club’s immediate priority is to first determine the futures of Neuer and Sven Ulreich before deciding whether, and when, to make a move for another goalkeeper. So, while there is still plenty to be decided, the early picture suggests Bayern Munich is preparing for a post-Neuer era with Urbig as the long-term No. 1, supported by an experienced backup rather than another young goalkeeper fighting for his position.
